# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 47 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_047_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 4 — The Devil Fears the Faithful

**47:1** I asked him again whether the commandments that had been given could also be kept by those who live in the world. He said: "They can be kept. For I commanded them and handed them over to those of you who are in the world. But I tell you: if you keep them and add no evil desires to them, you shall live. But if you add to them even a little of the desires of the world, you will not be able to keep these commandments."

**47:2** He said to me further: "I will also make known to you the workings of the devil, for he too has works that are evil. When a righteous man approaches, the devil is afraid of him. But when a double-minded and faint-hearted man approaches, the devil is not afraid of him at all, but immediately enters into him."

**47:3** "The man who is full of faith stands firm against the devil and is not afraid of him, for he has the Lord with him and the power of God. But the double-minded man is afraid of the devil and comes under his influence without difficulty, for the devil enters into that man and does with him whatever he wills."

**47:4** "Now the Lord himself is the Angel of Righteousness, and he fortifies all who have faith in righteousness and in the doing of good deeds. Trust in him and you shall overcome the devil, for the devil has no power whatsoever against you. Only believe in God and trust in him, and the Lord will come and drive the devil from you and remove his power from you."

**47:5** "The devil has place and dwelling only among those who are double-minded — among those who waver and fear him, and who have abandoned their faith. So the devil comes back to these people, enters them, and carries out every evil work. But against those who have faith in their hearts, the devil cannot stand. Therefore this commandment has this power: the one who believes in God and does good will have great joy."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the spiritual warfare motifs of the Mandates.*
